messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: stan syntax
parts:
This is related to C/C++'s prohibition on . in variable names.  It could be worked around, but would be tedious.  Underscores are viable though if you want to use those instead.

In summary (this should be in the manual somewhere and maybe checked in the parser) variable names:
 - Must consist of only letters, numbers and underscores.
 - Cannot begin with a number.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan syntax
parts:
I hate dots in variable names. R and BUGS are
the only two systems I've ever seen use them.
They're illegal in Java, C++, Python and MATLAB.
What's worse, I'm used to their meaning either
member variable or member function access.

It would be easy to change the syntax to allow them,
but I'd really rather not. I could be convinced to
include them if everyone else thinks they're
important.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan syntax
parts:
The error message here is tricky because variables
get used in contexts that could also be a function
name or number or bracket.

model {
STATEMENT
...
}

where STATEMENT can be

a_1 ~ foo();
4.2 ~ foo();
(a + b) ~ foo();
{ a ~ foo(); }

So we cna have any of a variable (a_1), a numeric literal (4.2),
a complex expression ((a + b)), or a block ({ ... }). It can
also be just a close curly brace ('}') to end the block.

If I've seen an open brace ('{'), then I have to get a
statement of some kind or a close brace -- I doubt the error
message is that clear, nor do I know offhand how to make it
that clear (I'll think about it some more).
